summary.headline: MGL Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose 31.7% QoQ to INR343 crore and PAT to INR194 crore, but management says margins will be under pressure for 1-2 months.
summary.overview: Average sales volume reached 4.766 mmscmd, up 7.01% YoY and 2.01% QoQ, with CNG at 3.496 mmscmd (+9.74% YoY) and domestic PNG at 0.623 mmscmd (+9.09% YoY). Industrial and commercial volume fell 7.15% YoY to 0.648 mmscmd after a 20% government-directed cut. EBITDA from operations was INR343 crore versus INR260 crore in Q4, and PNG realisations on alternate-fuel-linked industrial and commercial pricing rose sharply. Management flagged that West Asia LNG disruption, withdrawal of pooled gas from around the second week of July, and force majeure on RLNG imports make Q2 margins hard to predict. Capex guidance was raised to INR1,500-1,800 crore for FY27.

segments.name: CNG
segments.commentary: Volume 3.496 mmscmd, +9.74% YoY; 26,007 vehicles added in the quarter, taking the base to over 1.31 million; 519 stations after one addition. Management guides 8-9% CNG volume growth if prices hold.

segments.name: Domestic PNG
segments.commentary: Volume 0.623 mmscmd, +9.09% YoY; 97,461 DPNG conversions in the quarter (cumulative 2.17 million); about 95,000 domestic connections added per management. Management says FY27 could reach 8-10 lakh connections if bottlenecks ease.

segments.name: Industrial and commercial
segments.commentary: Volume 0.648 mmscmd, down 7.15% YoY on a 20% government-directed cut; 291 customers added, taking the base to 6,198. Realisations rose INR27-32/scm QoQ (70-80% YoY per management), priced off LPG and FO/LDO.

segments.name: UEPL (Unison Enviro)
segments.commentary: Average volume about 0.322 mmscmd vs 0.224 mmscmd a year earlier (+30-35%); management sees potential of about 1.2 mmscmd.

segments.name: Non-CGD initiatives
segments.commentary: Long-haul LNG has 2 stations at about 5 tonnes/day, roughly breakeven. Battery initiative is on hold. EV 3-wheeler cargo start-up is not yet breakeven. CBG plant of about 350 tonnes MSW/day planned on MCGM land.

guidance_outlook: Long-run EBITDA endeavour of INR8-9/scm, but management says it is not achievable to predict for the current quarter; margins under pressure for at least 1-2 months.
CNG volume growth of 8-9% assumed if prices are maintained; long-run volume growth guided at 8-9%.
Capex for FY27 raised to INR1,500-1,800 crore, subject to manpower and material availability; management calls it preponing rather than raising total capex.
Dividend to be maintained at current level despite higher capex; management said it may borrow, as the company is currently zero-debt.
Q2 gas sourcing and volumes not guided; management says it is 'anybody's guess'. It may restrict supplies to industrial customers to around 80% of DCQ.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex of INR350 crore; FY27 capex guided at INR1,500-1,800 crore.
Domestic connections about 95,000 in Q1, the highest ever in a single quarter; daily connection pace could rise from about 1,000 to 2,000-3,000.
Potential of 3.8-4 million households; about 3.3 million already passed and about 2.3 million consumers served.
Cumulative pipeline length over 8,477.01 km after adding 156.57 km in the quarter.
Management said it has about 0.6 mmscmd of HPHT long-term contracts and has used about 0.2 mmscmd via IGX.
demand_pricing: Gas sourcing mix (company level): APM about 30%, NWG and pooled about 21-22%, HPHT about 14-15%, Henry Hub contract about 21-22%, rest Brent, IGX and spot.
Pooled gas priced about $12.5-13/MMBtu, Brent-linked about $13-14/MMBtu, spot touched about $20/MMBtu (spot share very small).
Pooled gas withdrawn from around the second week of July; Henry Hub volumes are under force majeure, so MGL is not receiving full contracted quantities.
CNG is about 40-45% cheaper than petrol and about 12% cheaper than diesel per management; CNG price increase of about INR5/kg taken from February.
Bus CNG demand is about 6,000 buses, roughly 0.14 mmscmd or 4-5% of CNG volume; STU and private fleet programme launched.

qa_highlights.question: What is the company-level gas sourcing mix and blended cost, and how does Q2 look?
qa_highlights.answer: APM about 30%, NWG and pooled about 21-22%, HPHT about 14-15%, HH about 21-22%; pooled $12.5-13, Brent-linked $13-14, spot up to about $20/MMBtu. Q2 supply not guided.

qa_highlights.question: What margin can be assumed if the West Asia conflict persists for three months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is very difficult to call; margins will be under pressure for at least 1-2 months until the crisis resolves, and gas cost may spike.

qa_highlights.question: Why was industrial realisation lower than commercial?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing is linked to alternate fuels: commercial to bulk LPG, industrial to FO/LDO. Commercial realisation rose 10-15% more than industrial QoQ; MGL also gives large industrial customers a discount. Raigarh has a 10% committed discount for the first 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is volume growth guidance changed from the double-digit view given last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the earlier view depended on CNG growth above 8-9% and industrial growth of 12-14%. With supplies curtailed, it may restrict supplies to about 80%, so near-term growth is uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: Will a debt raise be needed for capex, and will the dividend be affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is prepared to raise debt (currently zero-debt), dividend will be maintained, and cash flow is manageable.

qa_highlights.question: Are the battery and EV initiatives a priority?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Battery is on hold, with a restructuring underway. Management expects no sizeable time or money commitment for the next 3-5 years.

risks_watch: Gas supply and cost: pooled gas withdrawn from around the second week of July, Henry Hub volumes under force majeure, and spot LNG bought for about 15 days to 3 weeks; management says Q2 supply is 'anybody's guess' and it may restrict industrial supplies to about 80% of DCQ.

Margin path: management says margins will be under pressure for at least 1-2 months and the INR8-9/scm EBITDA endeavour is a longer-term aim, not a quarterly guide; watch whether Q2 EBITDA/scm holds up.
Volume growth: CNG growth of 8-9% depends on prices being held; industrial and commercial volumes depend on gas availability; prior double-digit view was qualified by the curtailment.
Capex and funding: FY27 capex raised to INR1,500-1,800 crore against about INR350 crore spent in Q1; company is zero-debt and has said it may borrow, which would be a shift in the balance sheet.
Domestic PNG connection pace: about 95,000 connections in Q1 with monsoon, plumber, meter and pipe bottlenecks; FY27 target of 8-10 lakh connections is conditional on easing these constraints.
key_quotes: Now it is anybody's guess that what may happen to the ongoing West Asia crisis.
Definitely, it will be under pressure for at least 1 or 2 months until this crisis gets resolved or some settlement happens.
So, it is only preponing the capex.
We are prepared to raise debt because if my CBG plants starts, we need money there as well.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on long-term volume growth and balance-sheet strength but cautious and often evasive on near-term margins and Q2 gas sourcing, repeatedly saying the outcome was not predictable while the West Asia conflict continued. Management also declined to give Q2 APM and sourcing volumes, and on the pooled-gas and Henry Hub shortfall it said the matter was not in its hands and it could only represent the case to government.
